card.title: You Handle the Evidence
card.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you explain my missing magician's receipt to the treasurer? You booked him.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You paid him. I only found his number.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ring him for a replacement. You've got the number.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He won't send a duplicate unless the treasurer emails him directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then draft her email and get her to send it. Copy yourself in so you can chase him.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 delegates receipt explanation; A3 uses B's phone contact and A5 assigns drafting plus chasing the evidence.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 only found the number prompts A3 calling it; B4 direct-treasurer requirement prompts A5 drafting her email.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects A's responsibility claim and B4 supplies an actual procedural constraint, shaping successive delegation.

heightening.evidence: B4 blocks direct replacement; A5 enlarges B's role into coordinating and monitoring the treasurer's request.

specificity.evidence: A1 magician's receipt and treasurer define a concrete administrative loose end, not generic reluctance.
